critical_code_review_comments: importer.normalize converts '**' to '' (strip bold) and markdown table rows into pipe-separated plain text; works for the fixture. Edge case: tables with escaped pipes '\\|' inside cells would be split incorrectly, but no such content appears in the ChatGPT fixture.

clean_url() replaces the first '&' with '?' only when the url has no existing '?'. For the fixture ('?v=ID\&utm_source=...'), after removing utm the url already has '?', so no swap needed — correct. Watch out if ChatGPT ever outputs 'youtu.be/ID&utm_source=...' (no '?'); current code would then rewrite to 'youtu.be/ID?' which is still a valid URL.

parse_course_text: module title is taken from m.group(2) of 'MÓDULO N: title'. When the title is on the next line (fixture style: '# MÓDULO 1\n## Competencias ...'), title_next kicks in and uses the next non-empty line — verified working for all 5 modules in the MD fixture.

The ChatGPT fixture places the module title inside a '## ' subheading that normalize strips to plain text — good. If a user pastes '# MÓDULO 1 — Título' on one line the group(2) regex also captures it correctly.
